Republicans. In the open 4th District, Amanda McKinney backs "energy dominance and independence" and blames state gas taxes and the Climate Commitment Act.

Democrats. Her opponent John Duresky blames the Iran war for fuel prices and tariffs for rising costs, saying "We've got to remove the tariffs."

Utilities. A public utility manager says the BPA increase will hit customers "dollar for dollar."

sections.heading: Electoral Impact
sections.html: Energy costs dominate the race to replace Dan Newhouse, where McKinney and Duresky advanced. The state gas tax adds about 55 cents a gallon and carbon credits about 50 cents, giving Republicans a state target and Democrats a federal one.

Trade.title: Washington: Trade (Fed)
Trade.subtitle: Tariffs, farm exports and Canadian trade

sections.heading: Issue Overview
sections.html: Washington is one of the most trade dependent states, with about two in five jobs tied to trade. Federal tariffs and retaliation have hit its farm exports and cross border visits from Canada.

sections.heading: Key Data & Trends
sections.html: Agricultural exports from Washington ports fell nearly 11% to $16.86 billion in 2025, and exports to China dropped over 34% to $453.9 million. Canadian passenger vehicle crossings into Washington fell more than 24% in early 2025. A state analysis projects up to 31,930 jobs lost over four years under full tariffs.

sections.heading: Partisan Stances
sections.html:
Republicans. In the 3rd District, John Braun says tariffs raised material costs for his business and "We need to be a little more thoughtful on tariff policy."

Democrats. Senator Patty Murray says the tariffs are hurting Washington businesses and border tourism.

Farmers. One grower says, "I do not know of one instance where it helped us," though blueberry and asparagus growers welcome protection.

sections.heading: Electoral Impact
sections.html: Trade shapes the 3rd District, one of the most competitive seats in the country, where Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez faces Braun. An oyster farmer there says her farm lost over half its international sales.

Healthcare.title: Wisconsin: Healthcare (Fed)
Healthcare.subtitle: Federal Medicaid cuts and marketplace costs

sections.heading: Issue Overview
sections.html: Federal Medicaid cuts and expired marketplace subsidies are squeezing BadgerCare enrollees, marketplace buyers and rural providers. The open governor's race offers a clear choice on how the state responds.

sections.heading: Key Data & Trends
sections.html: Nearly 20,000 Wisconsinites have lost Medicaid or CHIP coverage since H.R. 1 passed, and about 45,000 dropped marketplace plans after premiums rose, according to Protect Our Care. Doubling BadgerCare's income limit would make 55,000 to 75,000 more people eligible. The state budget included a historic Medicaid rate increase for hospitals.

sections.heading: Partisan Stances
sections.html:
Democrats. David Crowley campaigns on the need to expand BadgerCare and fund local health services. State Representative Tara Johnson says states lack money to "clean up all of the damage."

Republicans. Tom Tiffany voted for H.R. 1, against extending ACA tax credits and for stricter work requirements, but says health care would be a budget "priority" and backs upfront price disclosure.

Advocates. Protect Our Care, which supports the ACA, compiled the coverage loss figures.

sections.heading: Electoral Impact
sections.html: Marquette shows Crowley ahead 49% to 46% among likely voters, with Trump's approval at a record low 38%. Health care gives Crowley a direct line to Tiffany's congressional votes.

Immigration.title: Wisconsin: Immigration (Fed)
Immigration.subtitle: ICE enforcement and Wisconsin's dairy workforce

sections.heading: Issue Overview
sections.html: Wisconsin's dairy industry relies heavily on immigrant labour, while sheriffs increasingly partner with ICE. The governor's race offers opposite answers on cooperation.

sections.heading: Key Data & Trends
sections.html: A UW Madison survey found 70% of dairy farm labour is done by people living in the country illegally. ICE made about 1,700 arrests in Wisconsin from September 2023 to July 2025, with the pace rising, and the Dodge County Jail holds ICE detainees. Milwaukee County has not honoured ICE detainers since 2018.

sections.heading: Partisan Stances
sections.html:
Democrats. Crowley says he does not see "any scenario where we would want to partner with ICE" and that local officers should "focus on protecting local communities."

Governor. Outgoing Democratic Governor Tony Evers says he is "very concerned" about enforcement aimed at farmworkers and warns the state "will be destroyed economically" if undocumented workers leave.

Republicans. Tiffany pledges to "end sanctuary jurisdictions" and require local cooperation on criminal cases, and has the Fraternal Order of Police's endorsement.

sections.heading: Electoral Impact
sections.html: Immigration splits urban Milwaukee from rural dairy country. Crowley's lead among independents fell 11 points in a month, and the race is within the margin of error.
